note: Power Substation's three prop slots per 14 §10 ('Rectangular, breaker panel along the back wall, 2-3 transformer housings as cover' / 'one dedicated hiding spot near the panel as a fallback') and §4 ('an explicit switch-locked gate blocking the ladder upward'). The transformer housings and breaker panel had no coverage on the original v1 sheet and are load-bearing gameplay geometry (DL-18 M4: no safe Watcher crossing without mid-zone cover), so this card generated no geometry until DL-5's human direction-approval gate cleared. signal_tower_props_concept_sheet_v3.png (T-0257) is that coverage: PR #307 (commit 9757b16) propagated T-0257's board approval verdict (approved_by/approved_at, card moved to done via PR #291) into ASSET_PROVENANCE.md, whose row for the v3 sheet now reads 'APPROVED 2026-08-30'. transformer_housing_a_v1, transformer_housing_b_v1, and breaker_panel_v1 are generated via the committed cutout path (tools/comfy-client/src/comfy_client/cutout.py, sdxl_cutout_lora_v1.json), style LoRA soviet_brutalism_style_v1 @ 0.70 only -- no prop LoRA, per the 2026-08-30 human re-gate comment on this card. transformer_housing_a_v1's first attempt (seed 24501) matted to only 9.4% opaque -- a fragmented, mostly-transparent failure, not a usable prop -- and was re-rolled through several seeds (24511/24521/24531/24541/24551/24571 all rejected on visual review: fragmented, weapon-like drift, or disconnected pieces) before seed 24561 produced a clean solid rectangular tank (87.5% opaque). ART-DIRECTION CORRECTION (2026-09-02): both housings' initial committed sprites (seed 24561 for A, seed 24502 for B), while using the v3 sheet's own reviewed sub-panel prompt text verbatim, rendered in three-quarter/isometric projection (two box faces visible) -- matching how the v3 sheet's own sub-panel art depicts them, but violating @DennieSeth's direction posted on this card ('object should face the camera, no isometry or perspective'). Both prompts were amended to force a single flat front face (no geometry change -- same squat sealed grey-green box, same cooling fins/no-doors/no-legs description, only the framing language), and both seeds re-rolled: transformer_housing_a_v1 -> seed 24562 (23.96% opaque, clean flat single-face rectangle). transformer_housing_b_v1 -> seed 24562 against the front-elevation prompt first produced a clean flat rectangle too, but at 'mid-value grey-green' its 16px luma16 gap vs locker_v1 (82.01) was only 14.49, below the 15.0 P-3 floor; the prompt's colour was bumped to 'pale light grey-green ... noticeably lighter in value than surrounding concrete' (framing unchanged) and re-rolled again at the same seed, landing on the current committed sprite (18.3% opaque, gap 63.74). Both new sprites were visually inspected (10x nearest-neighbour upscale) and confirmed to show only a single flat front face -- no visible top or side face, no corner. breaker_panel_v1 is unchanged -- its first generation already rendered as a flat, camera-facing wall plate. The hiding-spot slot reuses the already-committed, already-provenanced locker_v1 (T-0201/T-0221) as-is -- not regenerated.

slots.note: Two housings committed (within the room's own 2-3 range per 14 §10). Both generated against the approved v3 sheet's own TRANSFORMER HOUSING A / TRANSFORMER HOUSING B sub-panel prompts, amended (2026-09-02) to force flat front elevation -- see the top-level note's ART-DIRECTION CORRECTION entry.

A switch-locked interactive gate object (14 §4), not a cover prop and not a hiding spot -- a player cannot take cover behind or hide inside a thin wall-mounted plate. Excluded from the P-3 cover/hiding 16px separation gate for that reason (the gate constrains cover-vs-hiding legibility only).

slots.slot: Dedicated hiding spot near the panel

gate_16px_separation.requirement: >= 15.0 luma16 gap between any cover/hiding pair co-located in this room (P-3)
gate_16px_separation.how_measured: 16px-longest-side Lanczos downscale + BT.601 mean luma over opaque pixels -- the same rule as test_signal_tower_prop_pack.py's _downscale_to_game_16px/_mean_luma, re-derived directly from the committed sprites by test_power_substation_room_manifest.py::test_gate_measurements_match_real_sprites. locker_v1's luma16=82.01 matches the figure already recorded in locker_v1.provenance.json and Ground Relay/Storage Cache's manifests (82.0) to within rounding. transformer_housing_a_v1/b_v1's numbers here reflect the 2026-09-02 art-direction-corrected sprites (flat front elevation, re-seeded) -- both changed from the previous committed sprites (see the top-level note's ART-DIRECTION CORRECTION entry).
gate_16px_separation.why_this_is_the_hardest_case: Unlike Ground Relay/Storage Cache (one cover prop, one hiding prop, reused sprites already proven), Power Substation places TWO cover-class props alongside the room's hiding prop, and the Watcher's sweep makes the cover-vs-hiding distinction load-bearing, not incidental. Both pairs clear the floor with comfortable margin (37.1 and 63.7) -- transformer_housing_b_v1's prompt was deliberately lightened during the art-direction fix specifically because its first flat-elevation attempt (mid-value grey-green) only cleared the floor by 14.49, below the 15.0 minimum; the current pale-light-value sprite clears it with a wide margin instead.

breaker_panel_not_in_gate: breaker_panel_v1 (prop_class=gate) is intentionally excluded from cover_hide_pairs_in_room above -- see the slot note.
non_regression: T-0221's and T-0223's existing five props and the test_signal_tower_prop_pack.py gate suite are unmodified by this card. locker_v1 is referenced, not regenerated -- byte-identical to the file T-0221/T-0223 shipped. No existing prop file was touched.
